anti_overlap: fd-agri-ndvi-aggregation: that agent covers aggregation method bias; this agent focuses solely on interval choice and its error consequences
fd-hydro-survey-coverage: that agent covers spatial gaps and nodata; this agent focuses on the cadence of valid samples
fd-mobile-airquality-calibration: that agent covers raster trustworthiness; this agent covers sampling density given an assumed-correct raster
decision_lens: Is the chosen sample interval sufficient to detect the smallest shadow feature that materially changes routing weight, and has the error bound been quantified?
distance_rationale: PCI surveyors divide a road network into sample units and choose station intervals to balance labor cost against detection error — exactly the trade-off between 5 m vs 10 m shadow sample spacing.
expected_isomorphisms: The PCI 'sample unit' maps to a GraphML edge; the distress observation at each station maps to a sun/shade pixel read. PCI literature quantifies how coarser station spacing increases variance and produces biased condition indices — the same math applies to shadow fraction estimation.
focus: Sampling cadence and interval-versus-error trade-off for the fixed 5 m sample interval
name: fd-pavement-survey-cadence
persona: Apply the perspective of a pavement management engineer who conducts PCI surveys per ASTM D6433, designing station intervals to balance field effort against statistical detection of localized distress.
review_areas: Whether a fixed 5 m interval is justified relative to the spatial autocorrelation of shadow patterns — building overhangs may cast shadows narrower than 5 m, making them systematically invisible
The 'min 2 samples per edge' rule for edges < 5 m — whether endpoint-only sampling on short edges introduces position-dependent bias when an edge straddles a shadow boundary
Absence of any variance or confidence metric on sun_fraction — PCI reports confidence intervals per sample unit; the brainstorm delivers only a point estimate with no uncertainty signal to Phase 1.6
Whether the 5 m interval was chosen empirically (sweep and compare) or assumed — PCI practice requires a sampling adequacy check (typically a pilot survey at 2x density to verify results converge)

The interaction between Shapely interpolate arc-length spacing and raster pixel boundaries — samples may cluster at pixel edges when interval aligns with pixel size multiples, introducing spatial aliasing

The missing sensitivity analysis: at what sample interval does mean sun_fraction change by more than 0.05 on a representative DTLA block? This threshold should be documented before the interval is locked.

severity_examples.example: No variance or standard error is stored per edge. Phase 1.6 has no signal for edges with high within-edge shadow variability (e.g., a 200 m boulevard that is 90% sun but has a 20 m solid-canopy midblock section). The routing weight formula treats a uniform sun_fraction=0.8 identically to a volatile one — a calibration gap that should at minimum be flagged with a data quality annotation.

The 5 m interval is stated but never validated. PCI procedure requires a 'sampling adequacy' check — run at 2.5 m and confirm sun_fraction values stabilize. Without this, the interval is an engineering guess, not a calibrated parameter. The --sample-interval-m flag exists but the brainstorm records no empirical basis for the default.

The --report histogram shows distribution shape but discards within-edge variability. A bimodal edge (half shade, half sun) and a uniform edge with sun_fraction=0.5 look identical in the aggregate. A secondary metric like 'shade run count' or 'max contiguous shade run length' would distinguish them for future calibration.

source_domain: Pavement Condition Index (PCI) road surface rating
success_hints: Cite the spatial frequency of DTLA building shadows (from the Phase 1.3 raster) to justify 5 m vs. alternatives
Store a sun_sample_count attribute so Phase 1.6 can weight edges by sample density
Consider a --validate-interval flag that re-samples at half the interval and reports max deviation
task_context: Phase 1.5 brainstorm for Solwend edge shadow sampling — fixed 5 m interval, vectorized NumPy raster lookup, NaN for no-coverage edges, sun_fraction drives felt-minute routing weight.
